title: Stored physical sample retained beyond its intended lifecycle
description: The physical sample is being transferred into long-term freezer storage. If retention periods, destruction triggers, or disposal procedures are not enforced for the stored specimen, the sample may remain available beyond the purpose for which it was collected and stored, creating a privacy threat through unnecessary continued possession of highly sensitive biological material.
assumptions: This threat applies if the storage workflow does not reliably enforce specimen retention limits or destruction-at-end-of-use requirements.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping: PA12.01 clearly fits the PANOPTIC activity for this storage flow, but the exact LINDDUN Pro tree node id for retention-related disclosure/content-unawareness style harms may vary by catalog version.

title: Insufficient access controls on stored physical samples
description: Once the physical sample reaches freezer storage, inadequate physical or procedural access controls could allow unauthorized staff or third parties to access, inspect, remove, or use the specimen. Because biological samples can reveal sensitive personal and genetic information, weak storage access control is a concrete privacy threat for this flow.
assumptions: Assumes freezer storage access is not strictly limited, monitored, and role-governed.
uncertainty_note: The PANOPTIC fit is strong, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node id under Non-compliance/Insecurity is approximate because tree numbering differs across versions.

title: Misconfigured permissions enable unauthorized handling of stored specimens
description: If permissions governing who may deposit, retrieve, transfer, or process stored physical samples are overly broad or incorrectly configured, personnel may handle samples outside authorized purposes. This creates a privacy risk by enabling unauthorized downstream use or disclosure of a sensitive biological specimen.
assumptions: Assumes storage operations depend on permission settings, procedural authorization lists, or equivalent controls that could be misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible threat for the destination datastore, though evidence of actual misconfiguration is not provided in the flow text; included as a realistic privacy threat pattern for the storage step.

title: Collection and storage of a biological sample creates highly sensitive data capture risk
description: Sending the physical sample into storage operationalizes the collection of biological material from the data subject. Biological samples inherently enable extraction of sensitive information, including identity, health, or genetic characteristics, so this flow carries a privacy threat insofar as sensitive specimen collection is being preserved for later access and use.
assumptions: Assumes the stored sample remains linked, linkable, or usable in relation to an identifiable individual.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC PA03.11 is strongly applicable because the flow explicitly concerns a physical sample. The exact LINDDUN tree node id for disclosure via collection of sensitive personal data is best-effort.

title: Re-identification risk from de-identified sample ID and metadata context
description: Although the flow is described as sending a de-identified ID for sample use, the identifier and accompanying sample metadata may still permit re-association with a specific data subject when combined with other information available in the wet lab or elsewhere in the workflow. This creates a re-identification threat despite removal of direct identifiers.
assumptions: Wet Lab may have access to quasi-identifiers, operational context, or linkage tables that could enable matching the de-identified ID back to an individual sample donor.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit PANOPTIC activity is PA05.01.01 because the core risk is reversal of de-identification. LINDDUN Pro tree node is approximate because PANOPTIC is being mapped onto LINDDUN trees rather than using the standard DFD-position method.

title: Insufficient de-identification before sharing sample identifier to Wet Lab
description: The flow explicitly shares a de-identified ID back to the wet lab, but if the de-identification process is weak, reversible, or leaves enough residual linkage information in the metadata, the sample may still be identifiable. This would undermine the intended privacy protection of the returned identifier.
assumptions: The data in this flow includes sample metadata in addition to the pseudo/de-identified identifier, and that metadata may contain quasi-identifiers or context that weakens de-identification.
uncertainty_note: Applicable if the de-identified ID or associated metadata is not robustly de-identified; if only a random code with no linkable context is sent, this threat may be lower.

description: Sending sample metadata from LIMS to Wet Lab may expose more information than is necessary for sample handling if the metadata payload is broader than the minimum needed to use the de-identified sample ID. Over-disclosure in this transfer increases the risk that protected information becomes accessible within downstream operations.
assumptions: The flow labeled 'Sample Metadata' may include fields beyond the bare minimum needed by Wet Lab.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on actual payload content. The flow description suggests a de-identified ID is included, but does not fully enumerate all metadata fields.

If its legitimacy, access scope, or privacy handling practices have not been adequately assessed, the transfer may create a privacy compliance and governance risk.
assumptions: Recipient vetting and role-based need-to-know controls are relevant for internal data sharing between LIMS and Wet Lab.
uncertainty_note: This is a governance-oriented threat inferred from the downstream sharing action rather than directly evidenced by the short flow description; included because PANOPTIC explicitly treats unvetted recipients as a privacy activity.

If retention limits, archival/deletion schedules, or end-of-use destruction controls are not enforced for this storage destination, personal genomic data may remain available longer than necessary, increasing privacy risk from future access, reuse, or disclosure.

uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC PA04.02 clearly fits if encryption is inadequate, but the DFD alone does not prove encryption is missing. Tree-node mapping is approximate.

title: Misconfigured filesystem permissions could expose stored sequence data beyond authorized recipients
description: Cluster filesystems often rely on directory, group, ACL, or mount-level permissions. If those permissions are misconfigured for this stored sequence data, other users, services, or projects may gain unintended ability to read, copy, or process the data.
assumptions: Assumes shared or administratively complex storage where permission errors are plausible.
uncertainty_note: Applicable when the cluster filesystem is shared; if it is isolated per project, likelihood may be lower. LINDDUN tree node is approximate.

Storing the raw data without adequate de-identification or minimization creates elevated privacy risk at the destination datastore.
assumptions: Assumes the sequence data relates to human subjects and is treated as personal or pseudonymized data rather than fully anonymous data.

title: Sequence data transfer to storage could be intercepted in transit

uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC PA03.07 is directly relevant to the transfer. The best-effort LINDDUN tree node for disclosure via interception is approximate.

uncertainty_note: Tree-node mapping is approximate because PANOPTIC's sensitive-derivation concept does not map cleanly to a single canonical LINDDUN Pro node.

uncertainty_note: This is a plausible downstream use threat, but confidence is lower because the flow description emphasizes transformation rather than decisioning or subject-specific actions.

description: Placing context-relevant research data in the data delivery DMZ may make it accessible in a less-trusted zone. If access controls on S13-A are insufficient for the sensitivity of the staged dataset, unauthorized parties may access or retrieve the data, causing privacy compromise.

uncertainty_note: This is a realistic threat for a staging datastore, but no direct evidence of misconfiguration is provided.

uncertainty_note: The flow indicates a delivery handoff, but not whether formal usage restrictions exist; included as a genuine governance threat tied to the sharing step.

This can enable privacy-harmful downstream handling, reuse, or sharing of genetic material beyond the intended research purpose.

uncertainty_note: Applies if downstream use agreements or stewardship constraints are weak or absent. Tree node is approximate.

assumptions: Assumes access to the publishing location is restricted in principle rather than fully public.
uncertainty_note: The threat is grounded in the destination store's access-control posture. The specific Nc tree node is a best-effort approximation.

title: Trusted recipients may be insufficiently vetted before data is made available
description: The flow description says the data is made available to researchers and trusted interested parties. If recipient legitimacy or trustworthiness is not actually assessed before granting retrieval access, personal data may be disclosed to parties whose access is inconsistent with the intended trust boundary.
assumptions: Assumes enrollment or authorization of recipient access depends on vetting rather than the data being openly published.
uncertainty_note: Applies if 'trusted interested parties' is an operational category requiring verification. If the publishing location is intentionally public, this threat may not apply.

title: Usage restrictions for downstream recipients may be absent or insufficient
description: Once data is published for retrieval, downstream researchers or other trusted parties may reuse, retain, or redistribute it beyond the intended research context unless clear and enforceable usage restrictions accompany access. This creates a privacy threat where recipients can handle personal data in ways not bounded by adequate agreements.
assumptions: Assumes the data is subject to downstream use limitations and is not fully unrestricted/open data.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine risk for publication/retrieval flows, but applicability depends on whether the shared dataset contains personal data and whether binding usage terms are expected.

title: Research data may be insufficiently de-identified before publication
description: Making research data available via a publishing location can expose individuals if direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers, or linkable attributes remain in the dataset. Even if the data is intended as context-relevant research data, inadequate de-identification before publication can permit identification or re-identification by recipients.
assumptions: Assumes the dataset contains or may contain personal data rather than only fully anonymous information.
uncertainty_note: Strongly plausible for research-data publication, but depends on the actual content of 'context-relevant research data'.

title: Published research data may be exposed to unintended or overbroad audiences
description: This flow explicitly makes context-relevant research data available for researchers and interested parties to retrieve from an externally managed publishing location. If the publishing location is broadly discoverable or access controls are weaker than intended, personal or insufficiently protected data within the research dataset could become generally accessible beyond the intended audience.
assumptions: Assumes the published research data may contain personal data or data that can still affect data subjects if disclosed, and that access/discoverability controls at the externally managed location may not fully match intended restrictions.
uncertainty_note: The flow description indicates intentional publication, so this is only a privacy threat if the dataset includes personal data, is insufficiently de-identified, or is exposed more broadly than governance intended. Best-effort tree node under Disclosure of information.

title: Publishing may occur without sufficient downstream usage restrictions
description: The trusted data recipient sends research data to an externally managed publishing location. If data use terms, redistribution limits, retention rules, or steward obligations are absent or insufficient, downstream parties may handle the published data in ways that exceed the original governance expectations.
assumptions: Assumes some restrictions are expected for this research data and that external publication requires explicit downstream obligations to preserve privacy protections.
uncertainty_note: This applies when publication is expected to be governed rather than fully open. Tree node is a best-effort mapping under non-compliance/policy-governance concerns.

title: Shared research data may be out of scope for permitted sharing
description: Sending context-relevant research data to a publishing location may exceed the scope originally authorized by policy, agreement, consent, or study governance if publication to researchers and interested parties was not within the allowed sharing context.
assumptions: Assumes there are governing limits on permitted sharing for the research data and that public or semi-public publication may not always be covered by those limits.
uncertainty_note: The threat depends on the actual legal/policy basis for publication. If publication is explicitly intended and authorized, this threat would not apply. Tree node is approximate.

title: Research data may be insufficiently de-identified before publication
description: Before making research data available from the external publishing location, de-identification may be inadequate to prevent identification or re-identification of data subjects by researchers or other interested parties who retrieve the dataset.
assumptions: Assumes the dataset includes data about individuals and is intended to be shared in de-identified or privacy-protected form rather than as directly identifiable records.
uncertainty_note: This is a strong concern for published datasets, but it depends on whether the flow actually contains personal data and whether robust de-identification has already been performed. Best-effort mapping under non-compliance/data handling quality.

title: Published data may enable re-identification of data subjects
description: Once context-relevant research data is made available through the externally managed publishing location, recipients may combine quasi-identifiers, rare attributes, or external datasets to re-associate records with specific individuals, defeating prior anonymization assumptions.
assumptions: Assumes the published data contains enough indirect identifiers or uniqueness to support linkage with other accessible sources.
uncertainty_note: This threat is derivative of insufficient de-identification and depends on the nature and granularity of the dataset. Tree node is a best-effort identification mapping.

title: Externally managed publisher's downstream practices may be insufficiently vetted
description: Because the publication target is externally managed, its actual handling of hosted datasets—including indexing, replication, analytics, retention, and onward disclosure practices—may not have been fully assessed before the data is made available for retrieval.
assumptions: Assumes the external publishing location is operated by a separate party or under separate administrative control with its own data handling practices.
uncertainty_note: Applies specifically because the destination is externally managed; if the publisher's practices have been contractually and operationally vetted, this threat may be reduced or inapplicable. Tree node is approximate.

title: Patient may receive outreach about a new record without any applicable privacy notice
description: The 3rd Party Previous Enrollment Entity informs the Patient that a new record has been added to their file. If this outreach occurs without an accessible notice explaining that such records may be created and that the patient may be contacted about them, the patient lacks transparency about the data action and resulting communication.
assumptions: Assumes the patient was not previously given a clear notice covering record creation and outreach by this third party.
uncertainty_note: Applies only if no prior notice covered this outreach; the flow description alone does not confirm absence of notice. Tree node is a best-effort generic Unawareness mapping.

title: Outreach may occur without obtaining applicable patient consent
description: This flow represents a third party proactively contacting the Patient regarding a newly added record. If consent was required for this kind of outreach, and it was not requested before the communication, the patient may be subjected to an unexpected privacy-impacting contact.
assumptions: Assumes the outreach channel, context, or governing policy requires consent for this communication.
uncertainty_note: Whether consent is legally or operationally required is context-dependent and not established by the flow description. Tree node is a best-effort generic Unawareness/consent-related mapping.

title: New record notification may rely on an unvetted source record
description: Because the message tells the Patient that a new record has been added to their file, a privacy risk exists if the underlying source of that record was not sufficiently vetted before the outreach. Contacting a patient about inaccurate or improperly sourced data can expose them to downstream privacy harms and loss of control.
assumptions: Assumes the newly added record originated from another source and may not have been validated before use in outreach.
uncertainty_note: The flow implies a new record exists but does not show whether its source was vetted. LINDDUN Pro tree-node mapping for non-compliance/quality issues is approximate.

title: Patient outreach may be triggered by inaccurate record data
description: If the newly added file record is inaccurate, notifying the Patient about it can propagate privacy harm by legitimizing erroneous data and potentially prompting follow-on use or disclosure. The quality of the data should be assessed before initiating outreach.
assumptions: Assumes the new record may contain inaccurate information and that outreach is based on that information.
uncertainty_note: This is a data-quality-dependent threat inferred from the phrase 'new record has been added'; the flow itself does not establish inaccuracy. Tree node is approximate.

title: Patient may be notified after a record is added before having a chance to influence the action
description: The outreach states that a new record has already been added to the patient's file. This suggests the action may have been executed before the Patient had an opportunity to object, configure preferences, or otherwise influence whether the record would be created or whether outreach would occur.
assumptions: Assumes the patient should have had some opportunity to affect record addition or notification preferences before the event occurred.
uncertainty_note: The flow only confirms post-hoc notification, not whether advance control was required or available. Tree node is a best-effort mapping for loss of user influence/awareness.

title: Queued tool selections may derive additional sensitive genomic inferences
description: The bioinformaticist's choice of analysis tools and queued jobs on Compute Nodes can trigger processing that derives new sensitive information from sequence data, such as health-related, ancestry, or other highly sensitive genetic characteristics beyond the original submitted dataset.
assumptions: This flow represents initiation of analysis jobs over personal genomic/sequence data, and the selected tools are capable of inferring additional sensitive attributes from that data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping: PANOPTIC fit is strong, but the exact LINDDUN Pro tree node is approximate because the prompt does not provide the applicable threat-tree subset for Dd.

title: Tool selection may enable use of sequence data for secondary purposes
description: By selecting particular bioinformatics tools and queueing jobs, the Compute Nodes may process personal sequence data for purposes unrelated to the original reason for collection, creating a privacy threat of internal appropriation or secondary use.
assumptions: Some selectable tools or workflows may support analyses outside the original study, diagnostic, or operational purpose for which the sequence data was provided.
uncertainty_note: Applies if governance does not tightly constrain which analyses are permissible; the flow description alone does not confirm whether such controls exist.

title: Queued analyses may process data outside approved scope
description: The bioinformaticist's ability to choose tools and submit jobs creates a risk that Compute Nodes process sequence data in ways exceeding consent, study protocol, or contractual limits, even without sharing the data externally.
assumptions: There are purpose, consent, protocol, or contractual boundaries on permitted analyses of the sequence data.
uncertainty_note: Strong PANOPTIC match if scope restrictions exist; exact Nc tree node is approximate because no node catalog was supplied.

title: Insufficient usage restrictions on available compute workflows
description: If usage restrictions for data processors and downstream compute workflows are absent or weak, Compute Nodes may accept and execute jobs that violate agreed data-use limitations for the sequence data.
assumptions: The environment includes data-use agreements, study restrictions, or processor obligations that should constrain available analyses.
uncertainty_note: This threat depends on whether enforceable data-use restrictions are expected in this environment; the flow alone does not prove their presence or absence.

title: Final clinical report exposed to an unauthorized requester
description: This flow delivers a final clinical report from the Clinical Result Generation App to a bioinformaticist. If authorization and report-level access controls are insufficient, the app could disclose a patient's final report to a staff member who is not permitted to view that result, exposing sensitive clinical/genomic information.
assumptions: Assumes the final clinical report contains personal and likely sensitive health/genomic data, and that access should be limited by role, case assignment, or need-to-know.
uncertainty_note: Mapped to PANOPTIC sharing/exposure because the privacy harm on this flow is unauthorized disclosure during report retrieval. Best-effort LINDDUN tree node only; exact node may vary by the threat-tree version used.

title: Insufficient access controls on report retrieval
description: The Clinical Result Generation App may not enforce adequate operational access restrictions when the bioinformaticist pulls the final clinical report. Weak role checks, missing case-based authorization, or overly broad permissions could allow inappropriate access to patient reports.
assumptions: Assumes report retrieval should be constrained to authorized workforce members under least-privilege principles.
uncertainty_note: This is a control weakness grounded in PANOPTIC insecurity rather than a confirmed exploit. LINDDUN Pro node is best-effort because non-compliance subtree labels differ across editions.

title: Final clinical report retrieved without adequate encryption
description: If the final clinical report is transmitted or session content is exposed without adequate encryption, sensitive clinical/genomic data could be observed by unauthorized parties during retrieval from the app.
assumptions: Assumes the flow may traverse a network or other environment where transport/session protection is required.
uncertainty_note: Applicable only if transport-layer or equivalent encryption is absent or misconfigured; the DFD alone does not confirm this implementation detail. Tree node is best-effort.

title: Authentication interference could enable improper report access
description: If authentication to the Clinical Result Generation App can be bypassed, spoofed, or otherwise undermined, an unauthorized party could retrieve the final clinical report while appearing to be a legitimate bioinformaticist.
assumptions: Assumes report access depends on an authentication mechanism whose integrity is security- and privacy-relevant.
uncertainty_note: Threat is conditional on weaknesses in the authentication chain; the flow description does not itself demonstrate such a weakness. Tree node is best-effort.

title: Recipient legitimacy for final report access may be insufficiently vetted
description: The app may release the final clinical report to a downstream recipient whose legitimacy, current role, or need-to-know has not been adequately assessed. This can result in inappropriate handling of sensitive patient information by an internal recipient who is not the proper audience for the report.
assumptions: Assumes not every bioinformaticist is automatically an appropriate recipient for every final clinical report.
uncertainty_note: This overlaps with access-control concerns but is framed as recipient vetting under PANOPTIC. Included because the flow is specifically a disclosure to a downstream human recipient.

title: Recording of identifiable genetic care recommendations in external EMR enables linkability
description: The flow records professional recommendations and clinical next steps about a patient's genetic care in the External EMR. Persistently recording this context-rich research/clinical information alongside EMR context can allow entries about the same patient to be linked across encounters, datasets, or care episodes.
assumptions: Assumes the External EMR stores these recommendations with patient-associated record context rather than as fully de-identified notes.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping from PANOPTIC recording to LINDDUN linkability; tree node chosen generically because exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for this flow context is uncertain.

title: Patient identity may be readily inferable from recorded genetic-care context
description: Even if the entry is framed as context-relevant research data, the combination of physician-authored recommendations, clinical next steps, encounter timing, and EMR context may make the patient directly or indirectly identifiable within the external EMR.
assumptions: Assumes the External EMR entry is associated with or can be correlated to patient record metadata, clinician identity, timestamps, or other case details.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-effort generic identifiability mapping; exact LINDDUN Pro node may differ.

title: Genetic research-context data may be stored in the EMR beyond established scope
description: The flow places context-relevant research data, including genetic physician recommendations and next steps, into an external EMR. If the EMR's authorized purpose, patient permissions, or data minimization rules do not clearly cover this research-context content, the store may process data types outside the permitted scope.
assumptions: Assumes there may be purpose limitation, consent, or governance boundaries between clinical EMR use and research-context documentation.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether this research-context documentation is explicitly permitted in the EMR's intended use and governing agreements.

title: Downstream usage restrictions for externally stored genetic recommendations may be insufficient
description: Once genetic-care recommendations are logged in the External EMR, downstream users and processors of that EMR data may access or reuse the information. If data use restrictions, role limitations, or recipient obligations are insufficient, sensitive genetic context can be used more broadly than intended.
assumptions: Assumes multiple downstream users, processors, or integrations can access External EMR contents.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to disclosure/data misuse; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree node is uncertain.

title: Genetic recommendation data may be retained in the external EMR longer than necessary
description: Recording genetic physician recommendations and next steps in the External EMR may result in long-lived retention of highly sensitive health/genetic context. If the data are not destroyed or archived according to lifecycle requirements, the retained record increases future privacy risk.
assumptions: Assumes retention schedules for this category of data may be longer than necessary or not specifically enforced for genetic/research-context content.
uncertainty_note: Actual risk depends on the EMR's retention policy and applicable legal/clinical recordkeeping obligations.

title: Recording detailed genetic physician recommendations in the EMR can create excessive sensitive data about the patient
description: This flow explicitly records the genetic physician's professional recommendations and clinical next steps into the Internal EMR. Because the content is context-relevant research data in a genetic setting, the recording may capture sensitive inferences, risk assessments, and recommended actions about the patient beyond what is strictly necessary for routine care, increasing the privacy impact of disclosure or later misuse.
assumptions: Assumes the recommendations include sensitive patient-linked genetic or research-context details rather than only minimal administrative notes.
uncertainty_note: PANOPTIC PA03.09 clearly applies because the flow is a recording action. The mapped LINDDUN tree node is best-effort only; this is a collection/processing privacy risk rather than a perfect fit to a canonical LINDDUN DFD-position node.

title: Unvetted accuracy of clinician-entered recommendations could propagate incorrect genetic-context data
description: The flow depends on the physician manually logging recommendations and next steps into the EMR. If the recorded content is incomplete, inaccurate, or insufficiently validated, the patient may be affected by erroneous sensitive records that are hard to detect or correct later, creating a privacy-relevant data quality and content integrity risk.
assumptions: Assumes there is no strong secondary validation or structured accuracy check at entry time for these research-context recommendations.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible quality/privacy threat for manual entry, but the prompt does not explicitly state whether validation controls are absent.

title: Research-context recommendation data may be processed in the EMR beyond the scope originally established
description: The flow stores context-relevant research data inside the Internal EMR. If research-derived or research-context recommendations are entered into the clinical record without clear scope boundaries, the data may later be processed for routine clinical, operational, or secondary purposes beyond the limits established for the original context, creating a privacy scope-creep risk.
assumptions: Assumes the data originates from or is shaped by a research context with narrower usage expectations than general EMR processing.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether the research-context data is governed by narrower source restrictions than ordinary clinical documentation.

title: Patients may not receive sufficient notice that genetic research-context recommendations are entered into the EMR
description: When a genetic physician records professional recommendations and next steps in the Internal EMR, the patient may not be adequately informed that research-context information or related recommendations will become part of the internal clinical record. Insufficient notice can undermine the patient's understanding of how sensitive information is documented and subsequently handled.
assumptions: Assumes applicable notice is required for placing this category of research-context information into the EMR and that existing notices may omit this detail.
uncertainty_note: The flow alone does not prove a notice deficiency; included because research-context genetic data often has heightened transparency expectations.

title: Physical sample retained beyond contextual retention limits
description: This flow retrieves the remainder of a physical sample from storage after contextual retention requirements have been met. That implies a privacy risk if the sample is still being held in storage past the point at which it should have been destroyed or otherwise disposed of. Retaining a biological sample beyond its justified lifecycle creates risk of later unauthorized analysis, reuse, or disclosure.
assumptions: The phrase 'once contextual retention requirements have been met' means the sample should no longer need to be retained and is being retrieved as part of end-of-lifecycle handling. The threat is located at the storage element because the privacy issue is continued retention of the specimen there.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit LINDDUN Pro node for over-retention/destruction is approximate; exact node naming may differ by threat-tree version.

title: Retrieved sample may be improperly destroyed and remain recoverable
description: Because this flow removes the remaining physical sample from storage after retention requirements have been satisfied, a genuine privacy threat is that destruction or disposal is incomplete, leaving the biological material partially recoverable or still analyzable. Residual recoverability of a specimen can enable later identification, testing, or secondary use outside the intended lifecycle.
assumptions: The retrieval action is a precursor to destruction or disposal of the remaining specimen.
uncertainty_note: The mapping to Nc and the exact LINDDUN Pro tree node is best-effort; this threat is grounded in PANOPTIC's improper destruction concept rather than a directly obvious LINDDUN flow-position pattern.

title: Remainder of physical sample may be retained beyond its authorized lifecycle
description: This flow places the remainder of a physical sample into the disposal item after contextual retention requirements are met. A privacy threat exists if the disposal step is not actually completed in a timely way and the sample remains available beyond the end of its permitted lifecycle, allowing further handling or analysis after it should have been destroyed.
assumptions: The disposed sample still contains personal or identifiable biological material and the disposal item is an intermediate store prior to final destruction.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort LINDDUN mapping for retention beyond lifecycle; exact Dd tree node may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Disposed physical sample may be recoverable due to improper destruction
description: A privacy threat exists if placing the physical sample remainder into the disposal item does not ensure irreversible destruction. Residual biological material could remain accessible or recoverable from the disposal container, enabling later testing, identification, or other secondary use.
assumptions: The disposal item does not itself guarantee final irreversible destruction and unauthorized parties could access or recover material from it before or during downstream waste handling.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-effort choice for improper destruction/recoverability; exact node id may differ across LINDDUN Pro materials.

title: Insufficient access controls on disposal storage could expose discarded samples
description: Because the remainder sample is transferred into a disposal data store, a privacy threat exists if access to that disposal container or storage area is not properly restricted. Unauthorized personnel could retrieve, inspect, or remove biological material that was expected to be in protected disposal handling.
assumptions: The disposal item/store can be physically or operationally accessed by multiple parties and samples remain privacy-relevant until final destruction.
uncertainty_note: Mapped via PANOPTIC insecurity for this disposal store; Nc tree node is best-effort because LINDDUN Pro node naming can vary.

title: Residual biological material retained on reused flow cell after sequencing run
description: Used flow cells may retain physical sample remnants after the sequencing run if cleaning/disposal practices are inadequate. Because the artifact remains in the data store and may later be reused, personal biological material associated with a prior data subject can persist beyond its intended lifecycle and become available for later recovery or analysis.
assumptions: The used flow cell can be reused or otherwise handled again after the run, and residual sample material on the flow cell can still reveal personal or genomic information.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping: the PANOPTIC fit is strong for retention beyond lifecycle (PA12.01), but the exact LINDDUN Pro tree node id may differ depending on the catalog version; 'Dd.3' is used here as an approximate disclosure-related retention/destruction node.

title: Incomplete cleaning leaves recoverable sample material on flow cell
description: Attempts to clean the used flow cell may be insufficient, leaving at least partially recoverable biological residue. A subsequent operator or process could recover DNA or other sample-linked material, resulting in unintended disclosure of personal information from the prior sequencing run.
assumptions: Cleaning is intended as the destruction/sanitization step for residual physical sample material on the flow cell.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is approximate; this is grounded in improper destruction/sanitization of residual sample material rather than in network/system disclosure.

title: Insufficient handling controls for used flow cells permit unauthorized residual-sample access
description: If operational controls around storage, cleaning, reuse, and access to used flow cells are inadequate, unauthorized personnel or downstream handlers may gain access to residual biological material remaining on the flow cell. This weak stewardship increases the chance of privacy compromise from leftover sample material.
assumptions: The environment includes multiple handlers or downstream users of the used flow cell, and access/handling procedures are relevant to preventing privacy harm.
uncertainty_note: Included because the flow description emphasizes best-practice cleaning to prevent leakage; however, the threat is somewhat control-oriented and may also be modeled under PA06/PA12 depending on system boundaries. Tree node id is approximate.

title: Derived context-relevant research data may reveal new personal information
description: This flow explicitly transforms raw sequence data into context-relevant research data. That processing can derive novel information about individuals, potentially including sensitive traits, health-related inferences, ancestry, or other attributes not present as explicit fields in the original dataset.
assumptions: Sequence data is personal data or can be linked to individuals, and the resulting research data preserves subject-level or otherwise attributable information.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit LINDDUN tree node selected under Disclosure of information; exact node mapping may vary because PANOPTIC processing threats do not always align cleanly to a single LINDDUN Pro node.

title: Stored derived research data may be exposed through insufficient access controls
description: The cluster filesystem stores context-relevant research data derived from raw sequence data. If access controls on the datastore are insufficient, unauthorized parties may access highly sensitive derived datasets.
assumptions: The filesystem holds subject-level or otherwise linkable research data and may be reachable by multiple compute jobs, users, or administrative roles.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node mapping is best-effort; exact LINDDUN Pro node for insecure access control on a datastore may differ.

title: Derived research data may be insufficiently de-identified before storage
description: Context-relevant research data created from raw sequence data may still permit identification or re-identification if de-identification, minimization, or aggregation are insufficient before being written to shared storage.
assumptions: The output data is intended to be less identifying than raw sequence data, or will be used/shared under assumptions of reduced identifiability.
uncertainty_note: Applies if de-identification is expected or claimed for this research dataset; otherwise this may be less applicable.

title: Derived research data may be retained beyond its necessary lifecycle
description: Writing derived research data to the cluster filesystem creates a retention risk if the data is not destroyed after the research purpose, processing job, or approved retention period ends.
assumptions: No automatic deletion, retention enforcement, or lifecycle management is guaranteed for this stored output.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort LINDDUN node mapping for retention/non-compliance; exact node may differ across LINDDUN Pro catalogs.

title: Clinical report exposure via third-party portal discoverability or overbroad access
description: Uploading the final clinical report to a 3rd Party Portal creates a privacy threat if the portal makes reports generally discoverable or accessible beyond authorized recipients, such as through weak sharing settings, predictable URLs, or overly broad role access. Because the report is a sensitive clinical artifact, unintended exposure would reveal highly personal health information.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores and presents uploaded reports to downstream users and that access scoping or sharing configuration may be broader than intended.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit PANOPTIC activity is sharing exposure on the destination portal. LINDDUN Pro tree node is approximate because exact node mapping depends on the product's threat-tree version.

title: Insufficient access controls on uploaded final clinical report
description: The uploaded final clinical report may be accessible to unauthorized users if the 3rd Party Portal lacks sufficient operational access controls, such as tenant isolation, role enforcement, least-privilege permissions, or proper authorization checks. This would enable inappropriate disclosure of sensitive patient information after upload.
assumptions: Assumes the portal is responsible for enforcing authorization over stored reports.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen as a best-effort disclosure/access-control fit; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Unvetted downstream recipient legitimacy for third-party portal handling

An insufficiently vetted portal operator or administrator may mishandle sensitive clinical data or permit unauthorized onward access.
assumptions: Assumes the portal is operated by a separate third party and due diligence may be incomplete or absent.
uncertainty_note: Applies only if third-party vetting is weak or undocumented; the LINDDUN node is approximate because non-compliance mappings are less direct in flow-centric analysis.

description: The final clinical report may be uploaded to the 3rd Party Portal without sufficiently defined contractual or operational usage restrictions governing processing, onward sharing, retention, and stewardship obligations. Without clear restrictions, the portal could handle the report beyond intended bounds.
assumptions: Assumes the portal is a third-party processor or recipient subject to data-use or processing agreements.
uncertainty_note: This is a governance/privacy threat grounded in downstream handling, but confirmation would require knowledge of the governing agreement. Tree node is best-effort.

title: Clinical report retained on portal beyond intended lifecycle
description: Once uploaded, the final clinical report may not be destroyed after its intended use or retention period, causing prolonged availability of sensitive health information on the 3rd Party Portal and expanding the window for misuse or unauthorized access.
assumptions: Assumes retention/deletion controls on the portal may be absent, weak, or misaligned with required lifecycle limits.
uncertainty_note: Retention risk is plausible for this storage flow, though evidence of an actual retention policy gap is not provided. Tree node is approximate.

title: Unauthorized report access due to insufficient portal access controls
description: The 3rd Party Portal stores and serves final clinical reports containing highly sensitive genetic information. If access controls on the portal are insufficient, a person other than the intended Genetic Counselor could download a patient's final clinical report, causing an unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the portal enforces authentication/authorization for report download and that weakness in those controls would expose report contents to unintended recipients.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort LINDDUN Pro mapping: PA04.01 clearly applies to this download flow, but the exact Dd tree node may vary depending on the threat tree version.

title: Clinical report disclosure if download transport or stored copy is insufficiently encrypted
description: During download of the final clinical report from the 3rd Party Portal to the Genetic Counselor, inadequate encryption in transit or at rest on the serving side could expose sensitive genetic and clinical data to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Assumes the report is transmitted electronically over a network and contains personal and potentially special-category health/genetic data.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine threat for the flow, but whether the primary weakness is transport encryption, storage encryption, or both is not specified.

title: Misconfigured portal permissions expose final reports beyond intended counselor access
description: If permissions on the 3rd Party Portal are misconfigured, final clinical reports may be downloadable by other users, roles, or tenant contexts beyond the assigned Genetic Counselor, resulting in oversharing of patient information.
assumptions: Assumes the portal uses role-, case-, or tenant-based permissions to control report downloads.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort mapping to disclosure of information; exact LINDDUN tree-node granularity is uncertain.

title: Unvetted recipient receives sensitive genetic report
description: The flow delivers a final clinical report from the 3rd Party Portal to an external recipient (Genetic Counselor). If the legitimacy or current authorization of that downstream recipient has not been adequately vetted, sensitive report data may be disclosed to an inappropriate or outdated recipient.
assumptions: Assumes recipient legitimacy can change over time and should be validated before release of the report.
uncertainty_note: The PANOPTIC activity fits the external-recipient context, but the exact applicable Nc threat-tree node is uncertain because LINDDUN Pro node naming varies by version.

If downstream privacy and stewardship responsibilities are not sufficiently communicated or assured, the report may be stored, forwarded, or reused in ways inconsistent with the patient's expectations or obligations governing the data.
assumptions: Assumes downloaded reports can leave the portal's managed environment and be handled in local systems or communications channels.
uncertainty_note: This is grounded in the download-to-external-recipient context; best-effort Nc tree-node mapping only.

title: Insufficient usage restrictions on counselor handling of downloaded report
description: If there is no adequate data use agreement or usage restriction governing the Genetic Counselor's handling of the downloaded final clinical report, the report could be further used, retained, or shared beyond the intended clinical purpose.
assumptions: Assumes the counselor acts as a downstream recipient whose permitted uses and disclosures should be contractually or organizationally bounded.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on governance arrangements between the portal operator and the counselor/organization; exact Nc node uncertain.

title: Final clinical report becomes accessible beyond intended audience
description: The download mechanism may expose the report in a way that makes it discoverable or accessible beyond the intended Genetic Counselor, such as through guessable links, shared work queues, or overly broad report availability in the portal.
assumptions: Assumes the portal presents downloadable reports through URLs, listings, or shared interfaces that could inadvertently broaden access.
uncertainty_note: Exposure is a plausible privacy threat for this flow, but there is no specific implementation evidence about discoverable links or indexing.

title: Clinician may derive additional sensitive inferences from shared context-relevant research/genetic data
description: The flow explicitly states that the Clinician retrieves the data with additional input and analysis. That creates a privacy threat that the recipient can derive novel sensitive information about the patient beyond the originally shared facts, such as new genetic risk interpretations, familial implications, or secondary health inferences.
assumptions: Assumes the context-relevant research data is or includes patient-linked genetic/clinical information and that the clinician performs additional analysis on it.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit LINDDUN tree node for disclosure from inference/processing is approximate; exact node may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro catalog.

title: Clinician can link shared data with other clinical sources to build a richer patient profile
description: Because the Clinician receives context-relevant clinical/research data and is expected to add further input, this flow enables multi-source profiling by combining the counselor-provided data with existing clinical records, family history, or other datasets, increasing the patient's linkability/profile richness.
assumptions: Assumes the Clinician has access to other patient records or contextual datasets that can be combined with this flow's contents.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN Pro tree-node mapping for PANOPTIC multi-source profiling is approximate.

title: Genetic Counselor may share data beyond the scope justified for this clinician interaction
description: This flow transfers context-relevant research data from the Genetic Counselor to the Clinician. A genuine privacy threat exists if the shared dataset includes more genetic, familial, or research-context detail than is necessary for the Clinician's stated retrieval and analysis purpose, resulting in out-of-scope sharing.
assumptions: Assumes minimization and purpose-limitation obligations apply and the dataset could contain broader research/genetic context than strictly needed by the Clinician.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is best-effort because LINDDUN Pro does not map PANOPTIC out-of-scope sharing one-to-one.

title: Genetic Counselor may disclose to a downstream recipient whose privacy stewardship is insufficiently vetted
description: The flow depends on the Genetic Counselor trusting the Clinician as a downstream recipient of sensitive genetic/clinical data. If the clinician's legitimacy, access context, or privacy handling responsibilities are not adequately assessed for this particular transfer, the disclosure can create a privacy threat through unvetted recipient handling.
assumptions: Assumes recipient vetting is not automatically guaranteed merely because both actors are legitimate healthcare participants; context-specific authorization still matters.
uncertainty_note: Exact LINDDUN tree node for non-compliance/recipient vetting is approximate.

title: Clinician may further share or use the received data in ways inconsistent with usage restrictions
description: Once the Clinician receives the research-relevant clinical data, a downstream privacy threat is that the recipient could handle it inconsistently with any data-use limits, research constraints, or contextual expectations attached to the original disclosure, amounting to misrepresentation of permitted downstream use/sharing.
assumptions: Assumes the disclosed data is subject to contextual restrictions, such as treatment-only, minimum necessary, or research-governance limits.
uncertainty_note: This is a downstream-use/share risk inferred from the handoff; evidence of an actual agreement is not provided, so applicability depends on whether such restrictions exist.

title: Residual genomic data recoverable after decommissioning
description: Wet lab devices being decommissioned may retain genomic or related personal data in storage media, caches, logs, firmware partitions, or removable components, such that the data remains at least partially recoverable after resale or disposal. This creates a privacy threat because information thought to be retired can later be extracted by subsequent owners or service personnel.
assumptions: The devices can store privacy-relevant digital data locally and decommissioning includes transfer, resale, disposal, or reuse outside the original trusted environment.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort LINDDUN Pro node mapping for improper destruction/remaining recoverable data; exact tree node id may differ in your catalog.

title: Privacy-relevant device data retained beyond end of lifecycle
description: If devices used for genomic processing are not wiped or otherwise disposed of at the end of operational use, personal data may persist beyond its intended lifecycle. Even before resale, such unnecessary retention increases the window for later disclosure or misuse.
assumptions: The device contains or may contain personal/genomic data whose intended lifecycle should end at decommissioning.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node mapping is approximate because PANOPTIC is being used instead of standard DFD-position analysis.

title: Insufficient decommissioning access controls and sanitization safeguards
description: The decommissioning workflow may lack sufficient operational controls to ensure only authorized specialists perform sanitization, verify completion, and prevent device release before privacy-preserving erasure is complete. Weak governance around this flow can result in devices leaving custody with recoverable personal data.
assumptions: Decommissioning requires procedural and technical controls such as authorization, chain of custody, and verification of sanitization before resale or disposal.
uncertainty_note: Applicable because privacy risk depends on decommissioning safeguards, but the exact LINDDUN Pro node for this control weakness may vary.

title: Residual patient/genomic data recoverable from acquired wet lab devices
description: A purchased or refurbished privacy-relevant wet lab device may still contain recoverable digital data from prior use. If storage media are not properly sanitized before acquisition, personal or genomic information associated with prior data subjects could be disclosed to the acquiring organization through the device itself.
assumptions: The devices include persistent digital storage or embedded logs/configuration/history that may contain personal or genomic data from prior use, and acquisition may occur from refurbishers or secondary channels rather than directly from the original manufacturer.
uncertainty_note: Best fit is PANOPTIC PA12.02 because the flow description centers on avoiding leakage from previously used devices whose prior data were not properly destroyed. LINDDUN tree node is best-effort; exact node may vary by library version.

title: Acquired device accepted from an unvetted source with unknown prior data-handling practices
description: If the organization acquires a wet lab device from a manufacturer, refurbisher, or reseller whose sanitization and privacy practices have not been assessed, the device may carry residual personal/genomic data or other privacy-relevant artifacts from previous contexts. The privacy threat arises from relying on an untrusted or insufficiently vetted source during acquisition.
assumptions: The acquisition process may permit devices from third-party refurbishers or resellers, and supplier due diligence may be incomplete or inconsistent.
uncertainty_note: This is supported by the flow's emphasis on acquiring only from the manufacturer or after refurbishment according to privacy best practices. Tree node is best-effort because Nc mappings are less standardized across LINDDUN Pro versions.

title: Downstream refurbisher or supplier not assessed for trustworthy privacy stewardship
description: A refurbisher or supplier involved in preparing the device for acquisition may be a downstream recipient/handler of personal or genomic data remaining on the device. If that party's legitimacy and trustworthiness are not assessed, privacy-relevant data could be mishandled, retained, or inadequately removed before the device enters the environment.
assumptions: Refurbishment can involve third parties that access device contents during reset, testing, repair, or resale preparation.
uncertainty_note: Applicable when refurbishment by third parties is part of the acquisition path. I chose origin at the data store because the risk concerns the acquired device and its data-bearing state, not the specialist as a person.

title: Refurbishment process not vetted for adequate downstream data-handling practices
description: Even when the supplier itself is known, the refurbishment process may not be assessed for whether it securely wipes storage, handles extracted data appropriately, or prevents reuse of data artifacts. Unvetted downstream processing can leave personal/genomic data on the device or expose it during refurbishment.
assumptions: The refurbished device passes through data-handling steps such as diagnostics, backup, imaging, repair, or wipe verification.
uncertainty_note: This is a strong fit if the acquisition process depends on refurbishment assurances. Tree node is approximate.
